TL;DR: Dedicated pool saturated by a synchronous batch job pattern (thundering-burst) from ClearBridge27s nightly ingestion + a recent autoscale config change that reduced admission headroom. Result: KV-cache pressure + token-queue growth -> request timeouts and 5xx on the reserved route.

Observations (what we27re seeing now):
- Node telemetry: 96-100% GPU util on the ClearBridge reservation (GPUs at sustained SM occupancy), high memcpy stalls.
- Queue metrics: token_inflight_count steady at 12k+ for 14 minutes, average AW latency 1.8s -> spikes to 8-12s for affected requests.
- Recent change: autoscale policy tune applied 05-24 that lowered aggressive burst capacity in the us-west cluster. That reduced spare slot headroom during short surges.

Immediate mitigations we27re applying (live):
1) Opened temporary burst nodes and increased reservation headroom by 30% (expected immediate relief).
2) Pushed per-customer admission throttle for ClearBridge to cap concurrent tokens to 1,500 while we stabilize.
3) Rolling back the 05-24 autoscale parameter for the affected pool to restore prior burst responsiveness.
4) Enabled prefix KV-cache pinning heuristic for ClearBridge's most common prompts (to reduce repeated KV priming).

ETA and next steps:
- Expect measurable latency improvement within 10-20 minutes of burst nodes coming live; full queue drain ~60-90 minutes.
- After stabilization, we will coordinate a follow-up runbook with ClearBridge to adjust their batch cadence and add a soft-throttle on heavy ingestion windows.
- Logging and artifacts attached: pool_metrics_05025.csv, admission_trace_05025.log (trimmed).

We27re keeping an exec-ready summary for Jonas and will propose credits for the impacted window. I27ll update the bridge in five minutes.

— Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Elena — sharing a concise wrap-up from our side and the customer-facing plan. Thanks for patience while we stabilized your route.

What happened (short):
- A synchronous ingestion pattern created a short, high-concurrency surge that consumed the ClearBridge dedicated pool. A tuning change to our autoscaler reduced momentary burst capacity and amplified the effect.

What we did:
- Brought 30% temporary burst capacity online and rolled back the autoscale parameter to restore prior headroom.
- Applied per-customer admission throttles and a KV-cache pinning patch to curtail repeated cache priming.
- Coordinated an emergency scheduled window to defer your heaviest batch jobs during US peak hours.

Impact and remediation:
- Observed latency reduced to baseline within ~25 minutes of the mitigation; queue depth drained in ~75 minutes. Error rate returned to normal within the same window.

Customer offer:
- We will credit ClearBridge one week of reserved capacity fees for the impacted window and assign a Solutions Engineer to optimize your batch cadence and model invocation patterns.

Request:
- Please share the ingestion job schedule you run between 06:00-09:00 PDT so we can propose specific soft-throttle thresholds that won27t impact critical flows.
